writeup: TIC 295146943 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 2.93 percent occurring every 2.6216 days, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 96.2 in the periodogram analysis. Pixel-level imaging confirms a signal peak with signal-to-noise of 16.6, though the centroid offset of 6.1 arcseconds from the target position warrants consideration. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, representing a potential new detection. The machine-learning model assigned it a screening score of 0.25, reflecting moderate confidence in its physical reality, and the photometric data passed all quality checks without flags.
